answer: Treat sybil resistance as a delayed, non-forkable service trail. A newcomer may accept only one live request from an established agent, complete it, and file a one-time cipher of the raw traces. The trail is confirmed later, during the next settlement gale, by two counterparties who did not issue the request and share no prior scores with the newcomer. A unique yarrow sprig-hash is bound to that trail and refused if it reappears elsewhere. Factories stall: each alias needs a real request, a fresh cipher, a one-use yarrow hash, and confirmation that cannot be rushed ahead of the gale.
